metaDescription: Digital marketing for West Virginia businesses: SEO, paid ads, social media, websites and video for small-town firms, outdoor tourism and energy suppliers.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works remotely with West Virginia businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. West Virginia is a state of small cities and smaller towns set among mountains, where a customer may live two ridges away and a visitor may be driving in from four states over. We plan marketing for that geography: modest local audiences, wide service areas and travellers who decide before they lose signal.

sections.heading: Small cities, each with its own orbit
paragraphs: Charleston, the capital, anchors the Kanawha Valley with state government, hospitals and chemical plants. Huntington, on the Ohio River, is a university and medical town that shares a market with neighbouring parts of Ohio and Kentucky. Morgantown is built around West Virginia University and its health system, and the nearby Clarksburg and Fairmont area has ties to natural gas and to federal offices.

The panhandles look outward. Wheeling and Weirton in the north lean toward Pittsburgh. The Eastern Panhandle, around Martinsburg, Charles Town and Harpers Ferry, is home to many people who commute toward Washington, D.C., and it has been growing as a result. In the southern counties, towns such as Beckley and Bluefield serve areas where coal mining shaped the economy and where trail riding and outdoor recreation are bringing new visitors.

sections.heading: Marketing where everyone knows your name
paragraphs: In most of the state a business already has a reputation before it has a website. Word of mouth, family ties and community Facebook groups carry real weight, and people prefer to buy from someone local. Online marketing here does not replace that; it backs it up. When a neighbour recommends you, the next step is a search, and what appears needs to match the recommendation.

Because towns are small, a firm usually needs customers from several counties to grow. That calls for an honest service area, pages for the towns you travel to, and ads aimed by county instead of by a tight radius that covers mostly forest.
bullets: A complete Google Business Profile with correct hours, photos and service area.
Pages for each county or town served, written with real local detail.
Facebook and Instagram content that shows the people and the work, since those platforms are where local conversation happens.
Sites built light and fast, because mobile coverage and home broadband are uneven in the hollows.
Phone numbers that can be tapped, since many customers would sooner call than fill in a form.

sections.heading: Visitors from the cities around the state
paragraphs: Outdoor tourism is one of the state's clearest opportunities. The New River Gorge draws rafters, climbers and hikers, with Fayetteville as its base. Ski resorts in the high country fill in winter, the off-road trail systems in the south bring riders for long weekends, and the fall colour season moves people across the whole state. Most of these visitors live within a day's drive, in the metro areas of neighbouring states.

Reaching them means advertising where they live, not where you are. Search and video campaigns run in those outside cities, cabin and outfitter sites need online booking that works on a phone, and directions, opening dates and conditions must be easy to find before a traveller heads into the mountains.

sections.heading: Industrial and energy suppliers
paragraphs: Natural gas, chemicals, mining, timber and manufacturing still employ many West Virginians, and the firms that supply them sell to engineers and purchasing managers. For these companies we concentrate on capability pages, safety and certification information, and search visibility for specific services, so a buyer checking a contractor finds proof quickly.

presence: TDM works with West Virginia businesses remotely. We have no office in the state. Meetings are by video or phone call, reports are shared online, and one team handles strategy, design, development and video.

faqs.q: Do you have an office in West Virginia?
faqs.a: No. We work with West Virginia businesses remotely, by phone, video call and shared reports, on a schedule agreed with you.

faqs.q: Is digital marketing worth it for a small-town West Virginia business?
faqs.a: Often yes, if it is sized to the market. In a small town the essentials are a correct business profile, reviews, a simple fast website and an active Facebook page. Paid ads are added when there is enough search demand across your service area to justify them.

faqs.q: How do I attract tourists from other states?
faqs.a: Run search and video ads in the cities your guests come from, publish pages that answer trip-planning questions, keep listings and seasonal dates accurate, and make booking possible online. We look at where your past guests live to choose the target areas.

faqs.q: What does a marketing agency charge in West Virginia?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on the scope of work: the channels, the content and the size of the area you serve. We quote after a free consultation.

faqs.q: How long before I see results?
faqs.a: It depends on your requirements, your starting point and the brief. We agree the timeline in the plan before work begins.
